Minesweeper Controls

Reveal squares, place flags, and use chord clicks on desktop or mobile.

Play MinesweeperRulesStrategy

Mouse controls

InputActionWhen to use it
Left clickRevealOpen a square you believe is safe.
Right clickFlag or unflagMark a square that logic proves contains a mine.
Click an open numberChordReveal its remaining covered neighbors when the correct number of adjacent flags is present.

How chord click works

If an open 2 touches exactly two flags, clicking that 2 opens every other covered neighbor at once. Chording saves time, but a wrong flag can make it open a mine. Verify the flags before using it.

Chord does nothing when the adjacent flag count does not match the number. This prevents an accidental bulk reveal before the count is ready.

Mobile and touch controls

Use the visible Mode: Reveal button to switch between Reveal and Flag. In Reveal mode, a tap opens a square. In Flag mode, a tap places or removes a flag. You can also press and hold a covered square to flag it.

Tap an already open number in Reveal mode to chord. The board stays inside a horizontal scrolling area on larger difficulties, so you can move across an Expert board without resizing its cells.

Keyboard controls

KeyAction
← ↑ → ↓Move focus between board squares.
Enter or SpaceReveal the focused square, or chord an open number.
FFlag or unflag the focused square.
NStart a new game at the selected difficulty.
PPause or resume the current game.

Playing without a mouse

Use the arrow keys to reach a covered square, press F to flag it, and press Enter or Space to reveal. Focus remains on the board after each move, so you can continue navigating without switching back to the mouse.

Pause, restart and display controls

Pause covers the board and stops the timer. New game abandons the active game and creates a fresh seeded board. Dark mode changes the color scheme, while Fullscreen gives large boards more room. These display controls do not change the mine layout.

Common control mistakes

  • Do not flag a square only because it looks suspicious; flags should follow from the numbers.
  • Check every flag before chording an open number.
  • On touch screens, confirm the current Reveal or Flag mode before tapping.
  • Use Pause instead of leaving a timed game running in the background.

Use the controls while learning the rules and number patterns.
